claim: Down syndrome (DS) is caused by trisomy of human chromosome 21 (Hsa21).
source: Down syndrome (DS), caused by trisomy of human chromosome 21 (Hsa21), is the most common cause of congenital heart defects (CHD), yet the genetic and mechanistic causes of these defects remain unknown.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about the chromosomal basis of Down syndrome.

claim: Down syndrome is the most common cause of congenital heart defects (CHD).
source: Down syndrome (DS), caused by trisomy of human chromosome 21 (Hsa21), is the most common cause of congenital heart defects (CHD), yet the genetic and mechanistic causes of these defects remain unknown.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field of congenital heart defects.

claim: The genetic and mechanistic causes of congenital heart defects in Down syndrome remain unknown.
source: Down syndrome (DS), caused by trisomy of human chromosome 21 (Hsa21), is the most common cause of congenital heart defects (CHD), yet the genetic and mechanistic causes of these defects remain unknown.
evidence: This statement reflects the current state of knowledge in the field at the time of the study.

claim: Seven mouse strains with partial trisomies of regions of mouse chromosome 16 orthologous to Hsa21 were generated using chromosome engineering.
source: To identify dosage-sensitive genes that cause DS phenotypes, including CHD, we used chromosome engineering to generate a mapping panel of 7 mouse strains with partial trisomies of regions of mouse chromosome 16 orthologous to Hsa21.
evidence: The manuscript describes the experimental generation of these strains.

claim: The seven mouse strains accurately model DS CHD.
source: Using high-resolution episcopic microscopy and three-dimensional modeling we show that these strains accurately model DS CHD.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data using HREM and 3D modeling presented in the manuscript.

claim: Systematic analysis of the 7 strains identified a minimal critical region sufficient to cause CHD when present in 3 copies.
source: Systematic analysis of the 7 strains identified a minimal critical region sufficient to cause CHD when present in 3 copies, and showed that it contained at least two dosage-sensitive loci.
evidence: This is based on experimental analysis of CHD phenotypes across the mapping panel.

claim: The minimal critical region for CHD contains at least two dosage-sensitive loci.
source: Systematic analysis of the 7 strains identified a minimal critical region sufficient to cause CHD when present in 3 copies, and showed that it contained at least two dosage-sensitive loci.
evidence: This conclusion is derived from the mapping analysis showing that multiple non-overlapping regions are required.

claim: Two of the new strains model a specific subtype of atrio-ventricular septal defects with exclusive ventricular shunting.
source: Furthermore, two of these new strains model a specific subtype of atrio-ventricular septal defects with exclusive ventricular shunting and demonstrate that, contrary to current hypotheses, these CHD are not due to failure in formation of the dorsal mesenchymal protrusion.
evidence: This is based on experimental observations of heart defects in the mouse strains.

claim: AVSD with exclusive ventricular shunting in these DS models are not caused by failure in formation of the dorsal mesenchymal protrusion.
source: Furthermore, two of these new strains model a specific subtype of atrio-ventricular septal defects with exclusive ventricular shunting and demonstrate that, contrary to current hypotheses, these CHD are not due to failure in formation of the dorsal mesenchymal protrusion.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing normal DMP development in mice with AVSD.

claim: Congenital heart defects affect almost 1% of the population.
source: These affect almost 1% of the population and are a major cause of morbidity and infant mortality (Fahed et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Congenital heart defects are a major cause of morbidity and infant mortality.
source: These affect almost 1% of the population and are a major cause of morbidity and infant mortality (Fahed et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: The chance of being born with CHD is increased to approximately 50% in Down syndrome.
source: The chance of being born with CHD is drastically increased (to ~50%) in DS (Vis et al., 2009) in which a range of heart defects is seen, including ventricular septal defects (VSD) and outflow tract abnormalities such as overriding aorta (OA) and double outlet right ventricle (DORV).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: A range of heart defects is seen in Down syndrome, including ventricular septal defects (VSD) and outflow tract abnormalities such as overriding aorta (OA) and double outlet right ventricle (DORV).
source: The chance of being born with CHD is drastically increased (to ~50%) in DS (Vis et al., 2009) in which a range of heart defects is seen, including ventricular septal defects (VSD) and outflow tract abnormalities such as overriding aorta (OA) and double outlet right ventricle (DORV).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the types of heart defects in DS, supported by citation.

claim: Atrio-ventricular septal defects (AVSD) are often seen in Down syndrome.
source: Notably, defects that affect the atrioventricular (AV) junction, especially atrio-ventricular septal defects (AVSD) (Freeman et al., 1998) are often seen in DS.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: AVSD comprise a spectrum of cardiac malformations characterized by a common AV junction, guarded by an essentially common valve, as opposed to separate AV junctions guarded by mitral and tricuspid valves.
source: AVSD comprise a spectrum of cardiac malformations characterized by a common AV junction, guarded by an essentially common valve, as opposed to separate AV junctions guarded by mitral and tricuspid valves.
evidence: This is a definition based on established medical knowledge.

claim: People diagnosed with AVSD can present with communication between left and right heart chambers (shunting) at the atrial level (ostium primum defect) or at the ventricular level or with shunting at both atrial and ventricular levels.
source: People diagnosed with AVSD can present with communication between left and right heart chambers (shunting) at the atrial level (ostium primum defect) or at the ventricular level or with shunting at both atrial and ventricular levels (Mahle et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: The process of forming the AV junction involves the growth and fusion of a number of tissues from different precursor populations.
source: The process of forming the AV junction that divides the embryonic heart into a four-chambered structure involves the growth and fusion of a number of tissues from different precursor populations (Webb et al., 1998).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Tissues involved in forming the AV junction include the atrial and ventricular septa (mainly of myocardial origin), the mesenchymal cap of the atrial septum, and the superior and inferior endocardial cushions (endocardial origin).
source: These include the atrial and ventricular septa (mainly of myocardial origin), the mesenchymal cap of the atrial septum, and the superior and inferior endocardial cushions (endocardial origin).
evidence: This is established knowledge about cardiac development.

claim: The dorsal mesenchymal protrusion (DMP) was first described as the 'spina vestibuli' by Wilhelm His the elder in 1880.
source: In addition, the dorsal mesenchymal protrusion (DMP) first described as the 'spina vestibuli' by Wilhelm His the elder in 1880 (His, 1880; Mommersteeg et al., 2006) makes an important contribution to septation of the AV junction (Anderson et al., 2015; Snarr et al., 2007a; Snarr et al., 2007b; Webb et al., 1998).
evidence: This is supported by citations to historical and modern literature.

claim: The DMP makes an important contribution to septation of the AV junction.
source: In addition, the dorsal mesenchymal protrusion (DMP) first described as the 'spina vestibuli' by Wilhelm His the elder in 1880 (His, 1880; Mommersteeg et al., 2006) makes an important contribution to septation of the AV junction (Anderson et al., 2015; Snarr et al., 2007a; Snarr et al., 2007b; Webb et al., 1998).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: The DMP is a mesenchymal structure at the venous pole of the developing heart derived from the second heart field (SHF).
source: The DMP is a mesenchymal structure at the venous pole of the developing heart derived from the second heart field (SHF) and perturbations of its development result in AVSD (Briggs et al., 2013; Goddeeris et al., 2008; Rana et al., 2014; Tian et al., 2010; Webb et al., 1999; Xie et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: Perturbations of DMP development result in AVSD.
source: The DMP is a mesenchymal structure at the venous pole of the developing heart derived from the second heart field (SHF) and perturbations of its development result in AVSD (Briggs et al., 2013; Goddeeris et al., 2008; Rana et al., 2014; Tian et al., 2010; Webb et al., 1999; Xie et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: Abnormalities in the DMP have been detected in human fetal hearts with trisomy 21.
source: Abnormalities in the DMP have also been detected in human fetal hearts with trisomy 21, leading to the hypothesis that malformation of this tissue causes the AVSD in DS (Blom et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: There is a hypothesis that malformation of the DMP causes AVSD in Down syndrome.
source: Abnormalities in the DMP have also been detected in human fetal hearts with trisomy 21, leading to the hypothesis that malformation of this tissue causes the AVSD in DS (Blom et al., 2003).
evidence: This hypothesis is based on observations cited in the literature.

claim: Hsa21 carries 233 protein-coding genes (genome assembly GRCh38.p5).
source: Hsa21 carries 233 protein-coding genes (genome assembly GRCh38.p5) and it is thought that DS phenotypes result from an increased dosage of one or more of the genes on Hsa21.
evidence: This is based on genome assembly data.

claim: DS phenotypes are thought to result from an increased dosage of one or more of the genes on Hsa21.
source: Hsa21 carries 233 protein-coding genes (genome assembly GRCh38.p5) and it is thought that DS phenotypes result from an increased dosage of one or more of the genes on Hsa21.
evidence: This is the prevailing hypothesis in the field of Down syndrome genetics.

claim: Rare cases of partial trisomy 21 in humans have been used to identify critical regions that contain dosage-sensitive genes that when present in 3 copies cause DS phenotypes.
source: In humans, rare cases of partial trisomy 21 have been used to identify critical regions that contain dosage-sensitive genes that when present in 3 copies cause DS phenotypes (Delabar et al., 1993; Korbel et al., 2009; Korenberg et al., 1994; Lyle et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: Hsa21 shares synteny with a large region on mouse chromosome 16 (Mmu16) and with shorter regions on Mmu10 and Mmu17.
source: Hsa21 shares synteny with a large region on mouse chromosome 16 (Mmu16) and with shorter regions on Mmu10 and Mmu17.
evidence: This is established knowledge about chromosomal synteny between human and mouse.

claim: Ts65Dn and Ts1Cje were the first two DS models generated.
source: The first two DS models generated, Ts65Dn (Davisson et al., 1990) and Ts1Cje (Sago et al., 1998) have duplications of regions of mouse chromosome 16 (Mmu16) that are orthologous to Hsa21, and have been used to identify dosage-sensitive genes contributing to some DS phenotypes (Baek et al., 2009; Chakrabarti et al., 2010; Lana-Elola et al., 2011; Salehi et al., 2006; Sussan et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to the original publications describing these models.

claim: Ts65Dn and Ts1Cje have duplications of regions of Mmu16 that are orthologous to Hsa21.
source: The first two DS models generated, Ts65Dn (Davisson et al., 1990) and Ts1Cje (Sago et al., 1998) have duplications of regions of mouse chromosome 16 (Mmu16) that are orthologous to Hsa21, and have been used to identify dosage-sensitive genes contributing to some DS phenotypes (Baek et al., 2009; Chakrabarti et al., 2010; Lana-Elola et al., 2011; Salehi et al., 2006; Sussan et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Ts65Dn and Ts1Cje have been used to identify dosage-sensitive genes contributing to some DS phenotypes.
source: The first two DS models generated, Ts65Dn (Davisson et al., 1990) and Ts1Cje (Sago et al., 1998) have duplications of regions of mouse chromosome 16 (Mmu16) that are orthologous to Hsa21, and have been used to identify dosage-sensitive genes contributing to some DS phenotypes (Baek et al., 2009; Chakrabarti et al., 2010; Lana-Elola et al., 2011; Salehi et al., 2006; Sussan et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: Ts65Dn has additional aneuploidy of trisomy of 60 genes on Mmu17.
source: However, both models also have additional aneuploidy (trisomy of 60 genes on Mmu17 in Ts65Dn and monosomy of 7 genes on Mmu12 in Ts1Cje mice), making interpretation of their phenotypes difficult (Duchon et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Ts1Cje has additional aneuploidy of monosomy of 7 genes on Mmu12.
source: However, both models also have additional aneuploidy (trisomy of 60 genes on Mmu17 in Ts65Dn and monosomy of 7 genes on Mmu12 in Ts1Cje mice), making interpretation of their phenotypes difficult (Duchon et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Additional aneuploidy in Ts65Dn and Ts1Cje makes interpretation of their phenotypes difficult.
source: However, both models also have additional aneuploidy (trisomy of 60 genes on Mmu17 in Ts65Dn and monosomy of 7 genes on Mmu12 in Ts1Cje mice), making interpretation of their phenotypes difficult (Duchon et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation and represents a logical inference about the confounding effects of additional aneuploidy.

claim: The Tc1 mouse carries a freely-segregating copy of Hsa21.
source: Another DS model, the Tc1 mouse, carries a freely-segregating copy of Hsa21 and shows many DS phenotypes, including CHD (Dunlevy et al., 2010; O'Doherty et al., 2005), although the Hsa21 in this strain is not intact and the mice are mosaic for the human chromosome, again making interpretation difficult (Gribble et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: The Tc1 mouse shows many DS phenotypes, including CHD.
source: Another DS model, the Tc1 mouse, carries a freely-segregating copy of Hsa21 and shows many DS phenotypes, including CHD (Dunlevy et al., 2010; O'Doherty et al., 2005), although the Hsa21 in this strain is not intact and the mice are mosaic for the human chromosome, again making interpretation difficult (Gribble et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: The Hsa21 in the Tc1 strain is not intact.
source: Another DS model, the Tc1 mouse, carries a freely-segregating copy of Hsa21 and shows many DS phenotypes, including CHD (Dunlevy et al., 2010; O'Doherty et al., 2005), although the Hsa21 in this strain is not intact and the mice are mosaic for the human chromosome, again making interpretation difficult (Gribble et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Tc1 mice are mosaic for the human chromosome.
source: Another DS model, the Tc1 mouse, carries a freely-segregating copy of Hsa21 and shows many DS phenotypes, including CHD (Dunlevy et al., 2010; O'Doherty et al., 2005), although the Hsa21 in this strain is not intact and the mice are mosaic for the human chromosome, again making interpretation difficult (Gribble et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: The Dp(16)1Yey/+;Dp(17)1Yey/+;Dp(10)1Yey/+ mouse is the most complete mouse model for DS to date.
source: Thanks to recent advances in chromosome engineering, a number of mouse strains with duplications of regions of mouse chromosomes orthologous to Hsa21 have been generated, resulting in partial trisomies, including the most complete mouse model for DS to date (Dp(16)1Yey/+;Dp(17)1Yey/+;Dp(10)1Yey/+), which carries a duplication of all Hsa21-orthologous regions on Mmu16, Mmu17 and Mmu10 (Brault et al., 2015; Li et al., 2007; Liu et al., 2013; Liu et al., 2011; Olson et al., 2004; Pereira et al., 2009; Yu et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: The Dp(16)1Yey/+;Dp(17)1Yey/+;Dp(10)1Yey/+ mouse carries a duplication of all Hsa21-orthologous regions on Mmu16, Mmu17 and Mmu10.
source: Thanks to recent advances in chromosome engineering, a number of mouse strains with duplications of regions of mouse chromosomes orthologous to Hsa21 have been generated, resulting in partial trisomies, including the most complete mouse model for DS to date (Dp(16)1Yey/+;Dp(17)1Yey/+;Dp(10)1Yey/+), which carries a duplication of all Hsa21-orthologous regions on Mmu16, Mmu17 and Mmu10 (Brault et al., 2015; Li et al., 2007; Liu et al., 2013; Liu et al., 2011; Olson et al., 2004; Pereira et al., 2009; Yu et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: A comprehensive mapping panel to finely map dosage-sensitive genes in DS has not been available until now.
source: However, a comprehensive mapping panel to finely map dosage-sensitive genes in DS has not been available until now.
evidence: This statement reflects the novelty of the current work.

claim: The Dp1Tyb mouse strain carries a duplication from Lipi to Zbtb21 on Mmu16 spanning 23 Mb and 148 coding genes.
source: Thus we used long-range Cre/loxP mediated recombination to engineer the Dp1Tyb mouse strain carrying a duplication from Lipi to Zbtb21 on Mmu16 spanning 23 Mb and 148 coding genes.
evidence: This describes the experimental generation and characterization of the Dp1Tyb strain.

claim: Three strains with contiguous segmental duplications completely covering the region duplicated in Dp1Tyb were generated: Dp9Tyb (from Lipi to Hunk), Dp2Tyb (from Mis18a to Runx1) and Dp3Tyb (from Mir802 to Zbtb21).
source: We then generated 3 further strains with contiguous segmental duplications completely covering the region duplicated in Dp1Tyb: Dp9Tyb (from Lipi to Hunk), Dp2Tyb (from Mis18a to Runx1) and Dp3Tyb (from Mir802 to Zbtb21).
evidence: This describes the experimental generation of additional strains.

claim: Three strains with duplications breaking up the telomeric region of Mmu16 into three contiguous fragments completely covering the region duplicated in Dp3Tyb were generated: Dp4Tyb (from Mir802 to Dscr3), Dp5Tyb (from Dyrk1a to B3galt5) and Dp6Tyb (from Igsf5 to Zbtb21).
source: To increase the resolution of the mapping panel further, we generated another 3 strains with duplications breaking up the telomeric region of Mmu16 into three contiguous fragments completely covering the region duplicated in the Dp3Tyb strain: Dp4Tyb (from Mir802 to Dscr3), Dp5Tyb (from Dyrk1a to B3galt5) and Dp6Tyb (from Igsf5 to Zbtb21).
evidence: This describes the experimental generation of additional strains.

claim: Live mutant mice were recovered from all 7 strains.
source: We recovered live mutant mice from all 7 strains but noted that the yield of Dp1Tyb and Dp3Tyb mice was significantly reduced by 50% and 25% respectively (Table 1).
evidence: This is based on experimental observations of mouse breeding.

claim: The yield of Dp1Tyb mice was significantly reduced by 50%.
source: We recovered live mutant mice from all 7 strains but noted that the yield of Dp1Tyb and Dp3Tyb mice was significantly reduced by 50% and 25% respectively (Table 1).
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Table 1.

claim: The yield of Dp3Tyb mice was significantly reduced by 25%.
source: We recovered live mutant mice from all 7 strains but noted that the yield of Dp1Tyb and Dp3Tyb mice was significantly reduced by 50% and 25% respectively (Table 1).
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Table 1.

claim: Hydrocephalus was observed in Dp1Tyb mice around the time of weaning.
source: We also observed hydrocephalus in Dp1Tyb mice around the time of weaning, but not in any other strain (not shown).
evidence: This is based on experimental observations.

claim: Hydrocephalus was not observed in any strain other than Dp1Tyb.
source: We also observed hydrocephalus in Dp1Tyb mice around the time of weaning, but not in any other strain (not shown).
evidence: This is based on experimental observations.

claim: CGH confirmed the expected copy number increase (from 2 to 3) across the duplicated regions of Mmu16 in all 7 strains.
source: Comparative genome hybridization (CGH) confirmed the expected copy number increase (from 2 to 3) across the duplicated regions of Mmu16 in all 7 strains, with no other copy number changes seen in the genome (Figure 1b and data not shown).
evidence: This is based on CGH experimental data shown in Figure 1b.

claim: No other copy number changes were seen in the genome of the 7 strains besides the intended duplications.
source: Comparative genome hybridization (CGH) confirmed the expected copy number increase (from 2 to 3) across the duplicated regions of Mmu16 in all 7 strains, with no other copy number changes seen in the genome (Figure 1b and data not shown).
evidence: This is based on CGH experimental data.

claim: A significant increase of CHD was observed in E14.5 Dp1Tyb embryos compared to their wild-type littermates.
source: We observed a significant increase of CHD in E14.5 Dp1Tyb embryos compared to their wild-type (Wt) littermates (Figure 2a).
evidence: This is based on HREM analysis data shown in Figure 2a.

claim: About 18% of Dp1Tyb hearts show abnormal arterial trunk arrangements such as OA or DORV with subaortic communication.
source: About 18% of Dp1Tyb hearts show abnormal arterial trunk arrangements such as OA or DORV with subaortic communication and 62% had a VSD either alone or in combination with other defects (Figure 2b,c and Videos 1 and 2).
evidence: This is based on detailed examination of heart morphology data shown in Table 2 and Figure 2.

claim: 62% of Dp1Tyb hearts had a VSD either alone or in combination with other defects.
source: About 18% of Dp1Tyb hearts show abnormal arterial trunk arrangements such as OA or DORV with subaortic communication and 62% had a VSD either alone or in combination with other defects (Figure 2b,c and Videos 1 and 2).
evidence: This is based on detailed examination of heart morphology data shown in Table 2 and Figure 2.

claim: Two subtypes of VSD were observed in Dp1Tyb: perimembranous VSD (pVSD), located in the membranous portion of the ventricular septum and muscular or trabecular VSD (mVSD), which opens to the inlet of the right ventricle.
source: Two subtypes of VSD were observed: perimembranous VSD (pVSD), located in the membranous portion of the ventricular septum and muscular or trabecular VSD (mVSD), which opens to the inlet of the right ventricle (Figure 2c and Videos 3 and 4).
evidence: This is based on detailed examination of heart morphology shown in Figure 2c and Videos 3 and 4.

claim: Around 25% of Dp1Tyb embryos displayed AVSD presenting two bridging leaflets across the single AV junction and an 'unwedged' morphology of the left outflow tract.
source: Around 25% of Dp1Tyb embryos displayed AVSD presenting two bridging leaflets across the single AV junction and an 'unwedged' morphology of the left outflow tract (Figure 2c and Video 5).
evidence: This is based on detailed examination of heart morphology shown in Figure 2c and Video 5.

claim: The AVSD in Dp1Tyb mice were associated exclusively with a ventricular shunt and never with an atrial shunt.
source: Notably, the AVSD in Dp1Tyb mice were associated exclusively with a ventricular shunt and never with an atrial shunt (Video 6).
evidence: This is based on detailed examination of heart morphology shown in Video 6.

claim: Dp1Tyb mice model a subtype of AVSD with a ventricular component, in which the cushions are attached to the leading edge of the atrial septum.
source: Thus Dp1Tyb model a subtype of AVSD with a ventricular component, in which the cushions are attached to the leading edge of the atrial septum.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that AVSD in Dp1Tyb have exclusive ventricular shunting.

claim: Neither Dp9Tyb nor Dp2Tyb showed a significant increase of CHD compared to Wt littermates.
source: HREM analysis of embryonic hearts at E14.5 revealed that neither Dp9Tyb nor Dp2Tyb showed a significant increase of CHD compared to Wt littermates (Figure 3a).
evidence: This is based on HREM analysis data shown in Figure 3a.

claim: The telomeric duplication of 39 coding genes in the Dp3Tyb strain was sufficient to cause a significant increase in embryos with CHD.
source: In contrast, the telomeric duplication of 39 coding genes in the Dp3Tyb strain was sufficient to cause a significant increase in embryos with CHD.
evidence: This is based on HREM analysis data shown in Figure 3a.

claim: VSD such as pVSD, mVSD in the inlet portion of the ventricular septum, as well as AVSD were observed in Dp3Tyb.
source: We observed VSD such as pVSD, mVSD in the inlet portion of the ventricular septum, as well as AVSD (Figure 3b, Table 2 and Videos 7 and 8).
evidence: This is based on detailed examination of heart morphology shown in Figure 3b, Table 2, and Videos 7 and 8.

claim: A reduced frequency of outflow tract defects was noted in Dp3Tyb embryos compared to Dp1Tyb, however this difference was not statistically significant.
source: We noted a reduced frequency of outflow tract defects in Dp3Tyb embryos compared to Dp1Tyb, however this difference was not statistically significant.
evidence: This is based on comparison of data from Dp1Tyb and Dp3Tyb strains.

claim: The types of defects observed in Dp3Tyb were very similar in both type and severity to the ones in Dp1Tyb mice.
source: Overall the types of defects observed in Dp3Tyb were very similar in both type and severity to the ones in Dp1Tyb mice, suggesting that all the dosage-sensitive gene(s) required to cause CHD in Dp1Tyb mice were located in this shorter region.
evidence: This is based on comparison of phenotypic data from both strains.

claim: All the dosage-sensitive gene(s) required to cause CHD in Dp1Tyb mice are located in the Dp3Tyb region.
source: Overall the types of defects observed in Dp3Tyb were very similar in both type and severity to the ones in Dp1Tyb mice, suggesting that all the dosage-sensitive gene(s) required to cause CHD in Dp1Tyb mice were located in this shorter region.
evidence: This is inferred from the similarity of phenotypes between Dp1Tyb and Dp3Tyb.

claim: The Ts1Rhr strain does not show increased frequency of CHD.
source: Thus in order to eliminate possible confounding effects of background differences, we backcrossed Ts1Rhr to the C57BL/6JNimr background and used HREM to look for CHD. Once again we found no increased frequency of CHD in the Ts1Rhr strain (Figure 3c).
evidence: This is based on HREM analysis data shown in Figure 3c.

claim: An extra copy of one or more of the 8 genes duplicated in Dp3Tyb but not in Ts1Rhr is required to cause CHD.
source: Thus an extra copy of one or more of the 8 genes duplicated in Dp3Tyb but not in Ts1Rhr is required to cause CHD.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparison of CHD phenotypes between Dp3Tyb (which has CHD) and Ts1Rhr (which does not).

claim: None of the three strains Dp4Tyb, Dp5Tyb and Dp6Tyb showed significant increased rates of CHDs.
source: Next we analyzed Dp4Tyb, Dp5Tyb and Dp6Tyb mice each of which carry a duplication that between them cover the whole of the duplicated region in Dp3Tyb mice. Remarkably, none of these 3 strains showed significant increased rates of CHDs indicating that there are at least two dosage-sensitive loci in the Dp3Tyb mouse that contribute to CHD (Figure 3c).
evidence: This is based on HREM analysis data shown in Figure 3c.

claim: There are at least two dosage-sensitive loci in the Dp3Tyb mouse that contribute to CHD.
source: Next we analyzed Dp4Tyb, Dp5Tyb and Dp6Tyb mice each of which carry a duplication that between them cover the whole of the duplicated region in Dp3Tyb mice. Remarkably, none of these 3 strains showed significant increased rates of CHDs indicating that there are at least two dosage-sensitive loci in the Dp3Tyb mouse that contribute to CHD (Figure 3c).
evidence: This is inferred from the fact that Dp3Tyb has CHD but none of the three shorter duplications that together cover the Dp3Tyb region show CHD.

claim: A 4.9 Mb region of Mmu16 from Mir802 to Zbtb21 is sufficient when in 3 copies to generate cardiac defects similar to those seen in DS.
source: Taken together these data show that a 4.9 Mb region of Mmu16 from Mir802 to Zbtb21 is sufficient when in 3 copies to generate cardiac defects similar to those seen in DS.
evidence: This is based on the analysis of the Dp3Tyb strain.

claim: At least one of the two loci required for CHD resides within the 8 genes duplicated in Dp1Tyb but not Ts1Rhr mice.
source: Furthermore, the mapping analysis shows that there are two or more loci within this region that are required in 3 copies to cause CHD, and that at least one of these resides within the 8 genes duplicated in Dp1Tyb but not Ts1Rhr mice.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparison of CHD phenotypes between Dp3Tyb and Ts1Rhr.

claim: The Isl1 gene is expressed in the SHF and also in the DMP which is derived from it.
source: The Isl1 gene is expressed in the SHF and also in the DMP which is derived from it and hence can be used as a marker for this tissue.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Isl1 expression.

claim: Isl1 can be used as a marker for the DMP.
source: The Isl1 gene is expressed in the SHF and also in the DMP which is derived from it and hence can be used as a marker for this tissue.
evidence: This is inferred from the expression pattern of Isl1.

claim: At E11.5, there is an expansion of Isl1-expressing mesenchymal tissue from within the right pulmonary ridge, which forms the DMP and has started to protrude ventrally into the cavity of the right atrium.
source: At E11.5 analysis of both strains shows there is an expansion of Isl1-expressing mesenchymal tissue from within the right pulmonary ridge, which forms the DMP and has started to protrude ventrally into the cavity of the right atrium (Figure 4).
evidence: This is based on dual-wavelength HREM analysis shown in Figure 4.

claim: At E12.5, the DMP has protruded more ventrally and is now in contact with the inferior atrioventricular cushion.
source: One day later at E12.5, the DMP has protruded more ventrally and it is now in contact with the inferior atrioventricular cushion.
evidence: This is based on dual-wavelength HREM analysis shown in Figure 4.

claim: The expression of Isl1 diminishes later in development (E13.5) and totally disappears by E14.5.
source: Later in development (E13.5) the expression of Isl1 diminishes and totally disappears by E14.5 (Figure 4; Snarr et al., 2007b).
evidence: This is based on dual-wavelength HREM analysis shown in Figure 4 and supported by citation.

claim: By E14.5 the DMP forms the ventro-caudal buttress at the core of the AV junction sandwiched between the atrial septum and the endocardial cushions that have now developed into the tricuspid and mitral valves.
source: This revealed that by E14.5 the DMP forms the ventro-caudal buttress at the core of the AV junction sandwiched between the atrial septum and the endocardial cushions that have now developed into the tricuspid and mitral valves (Figure 4).
evidence: This is based on analysis using the Isl1Cre/Rosa26RLacZ fate reporter strain shown in Figure 4.

claim: At both E11.5 and E12.5 the DMP was present in Dp1Tyb embryos at a similar location to that seen in Wt mice.
source: We found that at both E11.5 and E12.5 the DMP was present in Dp1Tyb embryos at a similar location to that seen in Wt mice (Figure 5a).
evidence: This is based on imaging of the DMP using the Isl1nLacZ reporter strain shown in Figure 5a.

claim: At E11.5 in both Wt and Dp1Tyb embryos, the DMP appears rounded in shape and attached to the dorsal extracardiac mesenchyme.
source: Volumetric analysis showed that at E11.5 in both Wt and Dp1Tyb embryos, the DMP appears rounded in shape and attached to the dorsal extracardiac mesenchyme.
evidence: This is based on volumetric analysis of imaging data shown in Figure 5a.

claim: The size and shape factor of the DMP in Dp1Tyb mice at E11.5 was similar to that in Wt mice.
source: Furthermore, the size and shape factor of the DMP in Dp1Tyb mice was similar to that in Wt mice.
evidence: This is based on volumetric analysis of imaging data shown in Figure 5a.

claim: At E12.5 the size of the DMP was reduced in Dp1Tyb mice.
source: At E12.5 the size of the DMP was reduced in the mutant mice, but in both strains the DMP was more elongated and showed a similar shape factor (Figure 5a).
evidence: This is based on volumetric analysis of imaging data shown in Figure 5a.

claim: At E12.5 in both Wt and Dp1Tyb strains the DMP was more elongated and showed a similar shape factor.
source: At E12.5 the size of the DMP was reduced in the mutant mice, but in both strains the DMP was more elongated and showed a similar shape factor (Figure 5a).
evidence: This is based on volumetric analysis of imaging data shown in Figure 5a.

claim: The DMP was located in the correct position at the AV junction in both Wt and Dp1Tyb hearts at E14.5.
source: Finally, a more dorsal plane of the long axis view of the same hearts showed that the DMP was located in the correct position at the AV junction in both the Wt and the Dp1Tyb hearts (Figure 5b, right panels, and Video 6).
evidence: This is based on HREM analysis shown in Figure 5b and Video 6.

claim: The DMP was present in Dp3Tyb embryos with AVSD.
source: We performed the same analysis on the Dp3Tyb mice and once again found that the DMP was present in embryos with AVSD (not shown).
evidence: This is based on experimental analysis of Dp3Tyb mice.

claim: The AVSD found in Dp1Tyb and Dp3Tyb mouse models of DS are not caused by perturbations of the growth of the DMP.
source: Taken together these data show that the AVSD found in these new mouse models of DS are not caused by perturbations of the growth of the DMP.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that the DMP is present and largely normal in mice with AVSD.

claim: Defects in the DMP have been previously shown to result in atrial septal defects or AVSD with atrial shunting.
source: Importantly, we note that defects in the DMP have been previously shown to result in atrial septal defects or AVSD with atrial shunting (Briggs et al., 2012), neither of which are seen in Dp1Tyb or Dp3Tyb mice.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Neither atrial septal defects nor AVSD with atrial shunting are seen in Dp1Tyb or Dp3Tyb mice.
source: Importantly, we note that defects in the DMP have been previously shown to result in atrial septal defects or AVSD with atrial shunting (Briggs et al., 2012), neither of which are seen in Dp1Tyb or Dp3Tyb mice.
evidence: This is based on experimental observations of heart defects in these strains.

claim: Dp1Tyb and Dp3Tyb mice show AVSD with exclusive ventricular shunting.
source: In contrast these strains show AVSD with exclusive ventricular shunting, implying that this subtype of AVSD must be due to defects in tissues other than the DMP.
evidence: This is based on experimental observations of heart defects in these strains.

claim: AVSD with exclusive ventricular shunting must be due to defects in tissues other than the DMP.
source: In contrast these strains show AVSD with exclusive ventricular shunting, implying that this subtype of AVSD must be due to defects in tissues other than the DMP.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that the DMP is normal in mice with this type of AVSD.

claim: Approximately half of all babies born with DS have a heart defect.
source: Cardiac abnormalities are very common in DS. Approximately half of all babies born with DS have a heart defect, many of which are serious and need to be surgically repaired.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the prevalence of heart defects in DS.

claim: Many heart defects in DS are serious and need to be surgically repaired.
source: Cardiac abnormalities are very common in DS. Approximately half of all babies born with DS have a heart defect, many of which are serious and need to be surgically repaired.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the severity of heart defects in DS.

claim: The Dp(16)1Yey mouse strain carries a similar duplication to Dp1Tyb encompassing the same set of genes.
source: The Dp(16)1Yey mouse strain carries a similar duplication to Dp1Tyb encompassing the same set of genes and was also reported to have heart defects during embryogenesis (Li et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: The Dp(16)1Yey mouse strain was reported to have heart defects during embryogenesis.
source: The Dp(16)1Yey mouse strain carries a similar duplication to Dp1Tyb encompassing the same set of genes and was also reported to have heart defects during embryogenesis (Li et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: The cardiac phenotypes in Dp1Tyb are very similar to those observed in the Tc1 strain.
source: Interestingly, the cardiac phenotypes in Dp1Tyb are very similar to the ones we previously observed in the transchromosomic strain Tc1 (Dunlevy et al., 2010; O'Doherty et al., 2005), despite differences in the Hsa21 orthologous gene content in the two strains and the different species origin for the duplicated genes: mouse in Dp1Tyb mice, human in Tc1 mice.
evidence: This is based on comparison with previously published data on the Tc1 strain.

claim: The phenotypic similarity between Dp1Tyb and Tc1 supports the conclusion that the CHD seen in these strains are caused by the same pathological mechanisms as those in people with DS.
source: This phenotypic similarity supports the conclusion that the CHD seen in these strains are caused by the same pathological mechanisms as those in people with DS.
evidence: This is inferred from the similarity of phenotypes despite differences in gene content and species origin.

claim: Incomplete penetrance of CHD in humans with DS has been ascribed to genetic modifiers.
source: As with CHD in humans with DS we observed incomplete penetrance of the phenotype in Dp1Tyb mice. In humans this has been ascribed to genetic modifiers (Li et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: The Dp1Tyb mouse strain was analyzed on an inbred background.
source: However the Dp1Tyb mouse strain was analyzed on an inbred background, suggesting that incomplete penetrance may be caused by stochastic effects during embryonic cardiogenesis.
evidence: This is based on the experimental design of the study.

claim: Incomplete penetrance in Dp1Tyb may be caused by stochastic effects during embryonic cardiogenesis.
source: However the Dp1Tyb mouse strain was analyzed on an inbred background, suggesting that incomplete penetrance may be caused by stochastic effects during embryonic cardiogenesis.
evidence: This is speculated based on the observation of incomplete penetrance in an inbred background.

claim: The recovery of E14.5 Dp1Tyb embryos was consistent with expected Mendelian numbers.
source: While the recovery of E14.5 Dp1Tyb embryos was consistent with expected Mendelian numbers (not shown), the recovery of Dp1Tyb mice at weaning was reduced to 50% of the expected numbers (Table 1).
evidence: This is based on experimental observations.

claim: The recovery of Dp1Tyb mice at weaning was reduced to 50% of the expected numbers.
source: While the recovery of E14.5 Dp1Tyb embryos was consistent with expected Mendelian numbers (not shown), the recovery of Dp1Tyb mice at weaning was reduced to 50% of the expected numbers (Table 1).
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Table 1.

claim: Some of the perinatal loss in Dp1Tyb could be due to the most severe CHDs.
source: Some of this loss could be due to the most severe CHDs, since AVSDs were found in ~25% of E14.5 Dp1Tyb embryos, but it is likely that there are other unknown causes for this perinatal lethality.
evidence: This is speculated based on the frequency of severe CHDs.

claim: There are likely other unknown causes for perinatal lethality in Dp1Tyb besides CHDs.
source: Some of this loss could be due to the most severe CHDs, since AVSDs were found in ~25% of E14.5 Dp1Tyb embryos, but it is likely that there are other unknown causes for this perinatal lethality.
evidence: This is speculated based on the observation that CHDs alone may not fully account for the perinatal lethality.

claim: The Dp3Tyb strain showed a 25% reduction in recovery of mice at weaning.
source: The other strain to show AVSDs, Dp3Tyb, showed a 25% reduction in recovery of mice at weaning, similar to the observed frequency of AVSDs at E14.5, making this a likely cause of the reduced yield of mutant mice.
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Table 1.

claim: The reduced yield of Dp3Tyb mice at weaning is likely caused by AVSDs.
source: The other strain to show AVSDs, Dp3Tyb, showed a 25% reduction in recovery of mice at weaning, similar to the observed frequency of AVSDs at E14.5, making this a likely cause of the reduced yield of mutant mice.
evidence: This is inferred from the correlation between the frequency of AVSDs and the reduction in recovery.

claim: A previous study proposed that a 3.7 Mb genomic region of Mmu16 (Ifnar1 – Kcnj6) in Dp(16)4Yey was sufficient to cause CHD.
source: A previous study proposed that a 3.7 Mb genomic region of Mmu16 (Ifnar1 – Kcnj6) in Dp(16)4Yey was sufficient to cause CHD (Liu et al., 2013); this region overlaps the centromeric end of the duplicated region of Dp3Tyb by 1.9 Mb from Mir802 to Kcnj6, which may help to further narrow down the search for causative genes (Figure 6b).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: The Ifnar1 – Kcnj6 region overlaps the centromeric end of the duplicated region of Dp3Tyb by 1.9 Mb from Mir802 to Kcnj6.
source: A previous study proposed that a 3.7 Mb genomic region of Mmu16 (Ifnar1 – Kcnj6) in Dp(16)4Yey was sufficient to cause CHD (Liu et al., 2013); this region overlaps the centromeric end of the duplicated region of Dp3Tyb by 1.9 Mb from Mir802 to Kcnj6, which may help to further narrow down the search for causative genes (Figure 6b).
evidence: This is based on comparison of genomic regions shown in Figure 6b.

claim: The overlap between the Ifnar1 – Kcnj6 region and Dp3Tyb may help to further narrow down the search for causative genes.
source: A previous study proposed that a 3.7 Mb genomic region of Mmu16 (Ifnar1 – Kcnj6) in Dp(16)4Yey was sufficient to cause CHD (Liu et al., 2013); this region overlaps the centromeric end of the duplicated region of Dp3Tyb by 1.9 Mb from Mir802 to Kcnj6, which may help to further narrow down the search for causative genes (Figure 6b).
evidence: This is speculated based on the overlap of critical regions.

claim: In the Dp5Tyb strain, 2 mutant embryos with AVSDs were detected out of 20 embryos analyzed.
source: We note that while the Dp5Tyb and Ts1Rhr strains did not show a statistically significant increase in CHDs compared to their wild-type littermate controls, in both strains we detected 2 mutant embryos with AVSDs (out of 20 or 21 embryos analyzed respectively).
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Table 2.

claim: In the Ts1Rhr strain, 2 mutant embryos with AVSDs were detected out of 21 embryos analyzed.
source: We note that while the Dp5Tyb and Ts1Rhr strains did not show a statistically significant increase in CHDs compared to their wild-type littermate controls, in both strains we detected 2 mutant embryos with AVSDs (out of 20 or 21 embryos analyzed respectively).
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Table 2.

claim: It is possible that Dp5Tyb and Ts1Rhr strains have a weak CHD phenotype.
source: Thus it is possible that these strains have a weak phenotype – a larger number of embryos from these strains would need to be analyzed to establish whether this is significant.
evidence: This is speculated based on the observation of a few AVSDs in these strains.

claim: If Dp5Tyb and Ts1Rhr have a weak CHD phenotype, it would suggest that one or more of the causative genes may reside within the Dp5Tyb interval.
source: If true, it would suggest that one or more of the causative genes may reside within the Dp5Tyb interval (which is entirely contained within the Ts1Rhr interval).
evidence: This is speculated based on the potential weak phenotype in these strains.

claim: Analysis of humans with partial trisomies of Hsa21 identified distinct regions that contribute to cardiac abnormalities.
source: In contrast, analysis of humans with partial trisomies of Hsa21 identified distinct regions that contribute to cardiac abnormalities (Barlow et al., 2001; Korbel et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: An individual (PM) trisomic for the 7.7 Mb region from PSMG1 to PRMT2 had a VSD.
source: An individual (PM) trisomic for the 7.7 Mb region from PSMG1 to PRMT2 had a VSD, whereas the shortest partial trisomy (individual BA) that gave rise to AVSD extended 10.0Mb from HLCS to PRMT2 (Figure 6b).
evidence: This is based on human genetic data shown in Figure 6b.

claim: The shortest partial trisomy (individual BA) that gave rise to AVSD extended 10.0Mb from HLCS to PRMT2.
source: An individual (PM) trisomic for the 7.7 Mb region from PSMG1 to PRMT2 had a VSD, whereas the shortest partial trisomy (individual BA) that gave rise to AVSD extended 10.0Mb from HLCS to PRMT2 (Figure 6b).
evidence: This is based on human genetic data shown in Figure 6b.

claim: The duplicated region in individual PM does not overlap at all with the Ifnar1 – Kcnj6 region identified by Liu et al as being sufficient to cause CHDs.
source: We note that that while both of these intervals overlap substantially with the minimal Dp3Tyb region identified in our studies, the duplicated region in individual PM does not overlap at all with the Ifnar1 – Kcnj6 region identified by Liu et al as being sufficient to cause CHDs (Liu et al., 2013).
evidence: This is based on comparison of genomic regions shown in Figure 6b.

claim: Human studies suggested that increased dosage of the DSCAM gene may be responsible for the CHDs.
source: In particular the human studies suggested that increased dosage of the DSCAM gene may be responsible for the CHDs (Korbel et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Mouse studies show that duplication of Dscam is neither necessary nor sufficient to cause CHDs.
source: In contrast the mouse studies show that duplication of Dscam is neither necessary or sufficient to cause CHDs, since the gene is not within the minimal Ifnar1 – Kcnj6 region identified by Liu et al as being sufficient for CHDs (Liu et al., 2013) but is duplicated in the Dp6Tyb strain which we show here does not have CHDs.
evidence: This is inferred from the mapping data showing that Dscam is not in the critical region and that Dp6Tyb (which includes Dscam) does not have CHDs.

claim: Several dosage-sensitive genes may contribute to CHDs, with potentially no single gene being absolutely required.
source: Taking the human and mouse data together, this suggests that several dosage-sensitive genes may contribute to CHDs, with potentially no single gene being absolutely required.
evidence: This is speculated based on the combined analysis of human and mouse genetic data.

claim: Analysis of AVSD in people with DS showed that the most common subtype was a complete AVSD with both atrial and ventricular shunting.
source: Analysis of AVSD in people with DS showed that the most common subtype was a complete AVSD with both atrial and ventricular shunting and the next most common was AVSD with exclusive ventricular shunting similar to that seen in the Dp1Tyb mouse (Freeman et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: The next most common AVSD subtype in people with DS was AVSD with exclusive ventricular shunting similar to that seen in the Dp1Tyb mouse.
source: Analysis of AVSD in people with DS showed that the most common subtype was a complete AVSD with both atrial and ventricular shunting and the next most common was AVSD with exclusive ventricular shunting similar to that seen in the Dp1Tyb mouse (Freeman et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Dp1Tyb mice only model one subtype of AVSD seen in people with DS – AVSD with ventricular shunting.
source: Thus, although Dp1Tyb mice show AVSD, they only model one subtype of AVSD seen in people with DS – AVSD with ventricular shunting.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Dp1Tyb only shows AVSD with ventricular shunting.

claim: It is not known why some cases of DS have complete AVSD whereas others have subtypes with only atrial or ventricular shunting.
source: It is not known why some cases of DS have complete AVSD whereas others have subtypes with only atrial or ventricular shunting, but it is tempting to speculate that there are distinct mechanisms driving defects in the atrial and ventricular septa.
evidence: This reflects the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: There may be distinct mechanisms driving defects in the atrial and ventricular septa.
source: It is not known why some cases of DS have complete AVSD whereas others have subtypes with only atrial or ventricular shunting, but it is tempting to speculate that there are distinct mechanisms driving defects in the atrial and ventricular septa.
evidence: This is speculated based on the observation of different AVSD subtypes.

claim: A variety of different genetic manipulations that affect the DMP all resulted in AVSD with exclusive atrial shunting.
source: Importantly, a variety of different genetic manipulations that affect the DMP all resulted in AVSD with exclusive atrial shunting, demonstrating the importance of the DMP for the correct formation of the atrial side of the AV junction (Briggs et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: The DMP is important for the correct formation of the atrial side of the AV junction.
source: Importantly, a variety of different genetic manipulations that affect the DMP all resulted in AVSD with exclusive atrial shunting, demonstrating the importance of the DMP for the correct formation of the atrial side of the AV junction (Briggs et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature and represents an inference from the genetic manipulation studies.

claim: In Dp1Tyb mice there was normal DMP development and no AVSD with atrial shunting, but instead exclusively AVSD with ventricular shunting.
source: In contrast, in Dp1Tyb mice we found normal DMP development and no AVSD with atrial shunting, but instead saw exclusively AVSD with ventricular shunting (Figure 6c).
evidence: This is based on experimental observations shown in Figure 6c.

claim: Defects in the atrial septum causing the ostium primum type of AVSD are caused by malformation of the DMP.
source: Thus we propose that defects in the atrial septum causing the ostium primum type of AVSD are caused by malformation of the DMP, whereas ventricular defects are due to perturbations in other tissues, such as endocardial cushions or myocardium.
evidence: This is proposed based on the correlation between DMP defects and atrial shunting.

claim: Ventricular defects in AVSD are due to perturbations in other tissues, such as endocardial cushions or myocardium.
source: Thus we propose that defects in the atrial septum causing the ostium primum type of AVSD are caused by malformation of the DMP, whereas ventricular defects are due to perturbations in other tissues, such as endocardial cushions or myocardium.
evidence: This is proposed based on the observation that ventricular defects occur without DMP malformation.

claim: Gata4-deficient mice display AVSD and have a normal DMP.
source: Interestingly, Gata4-deficient mice display AVSD and have a normal DMP, but show perturbations in myocardial signaling to the adjacent atrioventricular cushion mesenchyme, suggesting that defects in myocardial signaling could lead to AVSD (Misra et al., 2014; Rajagopal et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Gata4-deficient mice show perturbations in myocardial signaling to the adjacent atrioventricular cushion mesenchyme.
source: Interestingly, Gata4-deficient mice display AVSD and have a normal DMP, but show perturbations in myocardial signaling to the adjacent atrioventricular cushion mesenchyme, suggesting that defects in myocardial signaling could lead to AVSD (Misra et al., 2014; Rajagopal et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Defects in myocardial signaling could lead to AVSD.
source: Interestingly, Gata4-deficient mice display AVSD and have a normal DMP, but show perturbations in myocardial signaling to the adjacent atrioventricular cushion mesenchyme, suggesting that defects in myocardial signaling could lead to AVSD (Misra et al., 2014; Rajagopal et al., 2007).
evidence: This is suggested based on observations in Gata4-deficient mice cited in the literature.

claim: The Dp1Tyb and Dp3Tyb mouse strains are the first to have been shown to have AVSD with ventricular shunting.
source: To our knowledge the Dp1Tyb and Dp3Tyb mouse strains are the first to have been shown to have AVSD with ventricular shunting and thus will allow direct studies of the pathological mechanisms underlying this subtype of AVSD.
evidence: This is based on the authors' knowledge of the literature.

claim: The Dp1Tyb and Dp3Tyb strains will allow direct studies of the pathological mechanisms underlying AVSD with ventricular shunting.
source: To our knowledge the Dp1Tyb and Dp3Tyb mouse strains are the first to have been shown to have AVSD with ventricular shunting and thus will allow direct studies of the pathological mechanisms underlying this subtype of AVSD.
evidence: This is inferred from the novelty of these models.

claim: The minimal critical region for CHD contains 39 protein-coding genes.
source: In contrast, the telomeric duplication of 39 coding genes in the Dp3Tyb strain was sufficient to cause a significant increase in embryos with CHD.
evidence: This is based on the analysis showing that the Dp3Tyb region (which contains 39 coding genes) is sufficient to cause CHD.

claim: The minimal critical region identified contains 8 genes (7 coding genes and 1 microRNA gene) that distinguish Dp3Tyb from Ts1Rhr.
source: To further narrow down the critical region for CHD, we analyzed embryonic hearts from the Ts1Rhr strain, which has a duplication that is shorter than that in the Dp3Tyb strain by just 8 genes (7 coding genes and 1 micro-RNA gene) (Olson et al., 2004).
evidence: This is based on comparison of the duplicated regions in Dp3Tyb and Ts1Rhr strains.

claim: The 8 genes that distinguish Dp3Tyb from Ts1Rhr are Setd4, Mx2, Tmprss2, Ripk4, Prdm15, C2cd2, Zbtb21, and Mir802.
source: By combining this data with analysis of the Ts1Rhr strain, we have determined that, minimally, one of the two loci lies either in an interval at the centromeric end of the duplication in Dp3Tyb (from Mir802 to Setd4) or at the telomeric end (from Mx2 to Zbtb21) (Figure 6a). These two segments between them contain only 7 coding genes (Setd4, Mx2, Tmprss2, Ripk4, Prdm15, C2cd2 and Zbtb21) and one microRNA gene (Mir802), none of which had been previously implicated in causing CHD in DS.
evidence: This is based on the genomic analysis shown in Figure 6a.

claim: None of the 8 genes (Setd4, Mx2, Tmprss2, Ripk4, Prdm15, C2cd2, Zbtb21, and Mir802) had been previously implicated in causing CHD in DS.
source: These two segments between them contain only 7 coding genes (Setd4, Mx2, Tmprss2, Ripk4, Prdm15, C2cd2 and Zbtb21) and one microRNA gene (Mir802), none of which had been previously implicated in causing CHD in DS.
evidence: This is based on the authors' knowledge of the literature.
